questions.q: How are the public seats at the back of the Court arranged?
choices: In tiers — the right for Europeans, the left for non-Europeans, 'according to the custom'
questions.explain: The chapter sets out at length the rules of respect owed to the Judge.

questions.q: What does the narrator say about the Judge and the Law?
choices: 'The Judge does not make the Law. It is the People that make the Law' — so an unjust outcome is the fault of the People, meaning the White People
The Judge can ignore an unjust law
The Law comes from the King alone
questions.explain: In a land of fear, the incorruptibility of the judges is 'like a lamp set upon a stand.'

choices: 'I plead guilty to killing, but I did not mean to kill' — which the court records as a plea of not guilty to murder
questions.explain: There is no charge of culpable homicide; it is murder or nothing.

questions.q: Who, according to Absalom's testimony, put forward the plan and chose the time?
choices: Johannes Pafuri, who said the time was told to him 'by a voice'
questions.explain: Pafuri also carried the iron bar, which he said 'had been blessed.'

questions.q: What did the three do on entering the kitchen?
choices: Tied handkerchiefs over their mouths; then Pafuri struck the servant Richard Mpiring once over the head with the iron bar
questions.explain: Mpiring had called out 'Master, master' before he was struck.

questions.q: What does Absalom say happened when the white man appeared in the passage?
choices: 'I was frightened. I fired the revolver' — and the white man fell
questions.explain: Then Pafuri said they must go, and they scattered into the plantation.

questions.q: Where did Absalom say he got the revolver?
choices: He bought it from a man in Alexandra; it had two bullets
questions.explain: He had fired one bullet earlier at a tree in the plantations, to prove it worked.

questions.q: What did Absalom do after burying the revolver in a plantation?
choices: He prayed there — 'I prayed for forgiveness'
He went straight to the police
questions.explain: The prosecutor seems 'taken aback' by this answer.

questions.q: When asked whether he had any reason for repenting other than being in trouble, what does Absalom say?
choices: That he feared for his soul
'No, I had no other reason' — he repented 'because I was in trouble'
That the priest had persuaded him
questions.explain: His plain honesty on this point becomes important at the sentencing.

questions.q: During Absalom's testimony, how do the other two accused behave?
choices: They 'look grieved and shocked to think such things are said' — maintaining they were not there
questions.explain: Absalom, by contrast, is 'still and silent.'
